quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Your arms give out halfway up, so do this to the wardrobe.
quests.explanation: 'Drop' implies it fell, whereas 'put down' is deliberate.
quests.textToSpeak: It took two of us to *carry* the wardrobe up the stairs.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Hikers do this when they head back to the car park.
quests.explanation: 'Descend' is formal; in conversation, 'come down' is usual.
quests.textToSpeak: We'll *climb* to the top in about an hour.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Wash a woollen jumper in very hot water and it will do this.
quests.explanation: 'Shrink' is irregular: shrink, shrank, shrunk.
quests.textToSpeak: Children *grow* so fast that clothes barely last a year.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: The shelf is bare, and the assistant says so.
quests.explanation: 'Sold out' is used for items completely bought up, like concert tickets.
quests.textToSpeak: The blue ones are *in stock*, so you can take them home today.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Empty wallet? Visit a cash machine.
quests.explanation: 'Take out' is the casual phrase: take out some cash.
quests.textToSpeak: I need to *deposit* some cash before the bank closes.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Someone who counts every coin at a group dinner.
quests.explanation: 'Thrifty' is positive, but 'stingy' is critical and informal.
quests.textToSpeak: Her uncle is *generous* with tips at restaurants.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Who walks at the front of a guided tour?
quests.explanation: 'Lead' is irregular (lead, led, led), and the verb rhymes with 'feed', not with the metal.
quests.textToSpeak: Just *follow* me — I know a shortcut.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Say 'I don't think so' to someone's idea.
quests.explanation: Agree and disagree both take 'with': I agree with you. We never say 'I am agree'.
quests.textToSpeak: Honestly, I *agree* with the manager on this one.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Your grandmother's dial telephone looks like this today.
quests.explanation: 'Outdated' is clearly negative, while 'traditional' is neutral or positive.
quests.textToSpeak: The hotel has a *modern* look, with glass and steel everywhere.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: You'll need a sharp knife and patience for this kind of steak.
quests.explanation: Tough and tender also describe people: tough means strong-minded, tender means gentle.
quests.textToSpeak: The steak was *tender*, almost melting in the mouth.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: When their team scores, fans do this.
quests.explanation: 'Scream' and 'yell' are even stronger.
quests.textToSpeak: The children were told to *whisper* during the film.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: A meeting that overruns by two hours.
quests.explanation: 'Lengthy' is mildly critical, while 'long' is neutral.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager asked for a *brief* summary of the report.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Put a concrete block beside a lovely park and describe the block.
quests.explanation: For people, 'plain' or 'unattractive' are kinder than 'ugly'.
quests.textToSpeak: The old town has a *pretty* little square.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Someone who falls for a trick without stopping to think.
quests.explanation: 'Silly' is playful; 'stupid' is stronger and can insult.
quests.textToSpeak: The fox was too *clever* to fall for the trap.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: After a bath, you pull out the plug.
quests.explanation: 'Empty' is the general word, but 'drain' stresses liquid flowing out.
quests.textToSpeak: The workers will *fill* the tank tonight.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Plans for a lazy Sunday.
quests.explanation: 'Rest' suggests recovering, while 'relax' suggests enjoying free time.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll *work* through the whole weekend.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Give a plant no water for months and it will be this.
quests.explanation: Before a noun use 'living' instead: a living creature.
quests.textToSpeak: The plant on my desk is still *alive*, thanks to a bit of water.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: What a court must declare before releasing a suspect.
quests.explanation: The real verdict is 'not guilty'. The feeling is also common: I feel guilty.
quests.textToSpeak: The jury decided that he was *guilty*.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Coins worth thousands usually are, since so few exist.
quests.explanation: A steak can be this too, meaning lightly cooked.
quests.textToSpeak: That bird is *common* here, so you'll see one soon.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: How you put out birthday candles.
quests.explanation: 'Inhale' and 'exhale' are the medical and yoga terms.
quests.textToSpeak: Now *breathe in* slowly through your nose.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: In a two-storey house, the front door is on this floor.
quests.explanation: After 'go' you need no 'to': go upstairs.
quests.textToSpeak: The bathroom is *upstairs*, next to the bedrooms.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: You wait for hours in an airport between two planes.
quests.explanation: 'Non-stop' means no landing at all, but a 'direct' flight may still stop briefly.
quests.textToSpeak: We chose a *direct* flight, even though it costs more.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Buy this ticket when you want to come home again too.
quests.explanation: British speakers say return; Americans say round-trip.
quests.textToSpeak: I only need a *one-way* ticket; I'm moving there.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: What you hope the departures board says about your train.
quests.explanation: 'Punctual' describes a person or service that is always on time.
quests.textToSpeak: The 8:15 train is *delayed* by twenty minutes.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Stepping into a warm café, you do this to your coat.
quests.explanation: Pronouns go in the middle: put it on, take it off.
quests.textToSpeak: It's cold, so *put on* your jacket.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: First job after arriving at the hotel, suitcase in hand.
quests.explanation: The prefix un- reverses many verbs, though not all: unpack, unlock, undo.
quests.textToSpeak: We'll *pack* tonight; the taxi comes at five tomorrow morning.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Once switched off, an oven does this over the next hour.
quests.explanation: Athletes warm up before exercise and cool down after.
quests.textToSpeak: Let the oven *heat up* before you put the cake in.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Someone sitting in the same café every single morning.
quests.explanation: 'Rarely' goes before the verb, but 'often' can also close the sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: I *rarely* eat out; I prefer cooking at home.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Night turns into day at dawn.
quests.explanation: 'Slowly' is the plain word; 'gradually' suggests steady progress.
quests.textToSpeak: The lights *suddenly* went out during dinner.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Explaining a slip you never meant to make.
quests.explanation: 'Accidentally' is the adverb; 'deliberately' means on purpose.
quests.textToSpeak: Did you delete those files *on purpose*?
